reasoning: Within the last 45 days, there appears to be only one publicly described general-election poll for Louisiana’s 2026 U.S. Senate race, commissioned by Democrat Jamie Davis’s campaign and conducted by Public Policy Polling in late July; it shows Republican Julia Letlow leading by about 4 points among registered voters, implying a narrow R+4 Senate margin at this time.[1] There is no state-specific 2026 presidential general-election polling in the results, and structural indicators such as Cook PVI rate Louisiana as a strongly Republican R+11 state, suggesting that absent contrary data, the default expectation for both Senate and presidential contests remains a Republican advantage.[3][5] Because most other recent items relate to primaries, national issues, prediction markets, or commentary rather than Louisiana general-election polling, they are treated as contextual rather than direct measures of the current race margin.

sources.name: The Bayou Progressive (reporting Public Policy Polling for Davis campaign)
sources.details: Campaign-commissioned Public Policy Polling survey of 518 registered Louisiana voters finds Republican Julia Letlow leading Democrat Jamie Davis 41% to 37% on the initial ballot, and 42% to 38% after biographical descriptions, indicating roughly an R+4 general-election Senate margin with about one-fifth of voters undecided.

sources.name: Cook Political Report (as summarized in Bayou Progressive article)
sources.details: Cook Political Report continues to classify the Louisiana U.S. Senate seat contested by Julia Letlow and Jamie Davis as Safe Republican, indicating a structurally strong GOP advantage in the state’s Senate politics despite the campaign’s internal poll suggesting a closer race.
sources.date_range: Not specified (Cook structural rating, not a poll)

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI (as reported via Wikipedia summary table)
sources.details: Cook Partisan Voting Index lists Louisiana’s statewide PVI as R+11, reflecting that in the last two presidential elections the state voted about 11 points more Republican than the nation as a whole, underscoring a strong baseline GOP advantage for both federal statewide races.
sources.date_range: Structural index based on 2020 and 2024 presidential results

sources.name: CBS News/YouGov via BizPac Review
sources.details: A CBS News/YouGov national poll cited in coverage of Sen. John Kennedy discusses U.S. attitudes toward ending the Iran conflict (67% favor ending the conflict vs. 33% favor continuing), but does not provide Louisiana-specific or 2026-statewide general-election results, so it is only contextual to Louisiana politics.

sources.name: The Hayride
sources.details: A commentary piece argues that despite the Davis campaign’s internal poll, Julia Letlow is likely ahead by at least 15 points and projects she will ultimately win the Louisiana U.S. Senate race by 15–20 points, reflecting a perception of a substantial Republican structural advantage but not reporting independent survey data.

sources.name: Louisiana Radio Network / World Population Review
sources.details: A Louisiana-focused article cites a World Population Review estimate placing former President Trump’s approval rating in Louisiana at about 49%, down nine points from five months earlier, which offers general partisan climate context but not a direct 2026 presidential or Senate head-to-head margin.
sources.date_range: Not specified (structural approval estimate, not a general-election ballot)
